reviews.review:
In the grim darkness of the far future, there are only Space Marine focused Warhammer media to sell you more of expensive toys to play with

TL;DR: It's okayish , short(5-6h) game. It's simplistic, extremely linear and has many issues that were present in that generation of games - like some disgustingly bad QTE. 
Without Warhammer name, it'd probably have been forgotten fast. But the Warhammer games being what they are, this is still one of the better games in that universe.  Because despite it's issues it IS fun to commit genocide against Orks and Chaos alike. Though I have my doubts if somebody would really like the game without being a 40k fan.

If you ever played other Warhammer 40k games or read 40k novels - you pretty much know what to expect. Bunch of grizzled, giant superhumans go against all odds, where stakes are so high they are silly. Like they are from child pretend game.
But that's what Warhammer is all about, so if you want that in a game form, you are at the right address. You play as Captain Titus of the Ultramarines chapter, because what other chapter would they pick. What helps that Titus doesn't worship Codes Astartes like other Ultramarines are usually portrayed to do.

Levels are simple, linear. I honestly have no idea what to even say about them, you just go forward. They do look their part, as they nailed how drab a manufacturing city would look in dystopian hellhole that 40k is. Everything is gray and samey, but it's functional and sets the mood well enough. 
Music is fine, has some better tracks, but otherwise it's just fine, just like the whole game. At some times it feels like it doesn't really fit the atmosphere, but that happens rarely.

On your Tour de Genocide you have a variety of typical 40k weapons to help you - bolters, plasma guns, chainswords or power axes. You know the stuff, there is nothing surprising here.  You always carry a melee weapon as well 4 ranged weapons, where one of the weapons is a pistol.  

There is no cover system, so you have to stay on your toes and keep moving. Game is essentially pushing you towards melee attacks - at least against orks. Against Chaos it gets more complicated, as their damage is much higher and most of it is from range. That's the part where gameplay starts to feel wrong and that it wasn't designed for these kinds of encounters, though having regenerating shield, which works as second healthbar essentially, helps a lot.  

Your melee weapons have combos - and each weapon has them the EXACT same. And there is no such thing are delayed input combos or movement based combos. You just mash melee attack button and maybe a stun button to stun enemies to ready them for the execution. Execution, which you might know with a "glory kill" name from DOOM 2k16, is the main way to restore your actual health. 

The issue with the Executions are multiple. One of them is a low variety of them, they get repetitive really fast. Another one is that you are still vulnerable and can easily die during them. That by itself is kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but some of the executions actually have different length - as in some take longer. Which one will happen? Who knows. Better pray it's the shorter one if you really need it.

The other way to restore health is "Fury". Fury is essentially a super mode, the "I win" button.  During Fury you regenerate health really fast and do increased damage. You can use Fury when you fill the Fury meter, which you do by doing damage. In a way, this feels more like a bandaid on some of the issues of combat system, but it does help.

Despite its issues, how clunky and shallow it feels sometimes, it is fun to just mindlessly button mash and see enemies explode into huge red mist. The responsiveness is really good - both in how fast and powerful Titus feels to control and how enemies respond to getting hit, with some satisfying sound effects. 

Bottom line is - if you want a 40k game that's not a strategy and want to take the action into your own hands, this is probably the best game. That doesn't mean it's anything more than "okay" or "fine".  There are some good ideas in this game, but badly executed. Hopefully, the second game will address that and it does look pretty good.
All who dislike this game, ARE HERITICS

Gave this is re-install since the sequel got announced. Still pretty fun for a short action game where you stomp around as a space marine.

Leandros is one of gaming's biggest losers.
